Kind: analysis only. Not residual invent. Not free / complete / PROVABLY /

---

## Operator question

> Do linear types help us make provably fastest C because there is no GC and there are no runtime libraries?

---

## Question split (what evidence counts)

| Piece | What evidence counts | What does not count |
|-------|----------------------|---------------------|
| **No GC** | Product wire consumer path has no GC library; structural `ldd`/`nm` honesty; freestanding-first compile of wire; contrast with Boehm arm that **must** show libgc when run | Compile-time vs Lake alone; residual free pin alone |
| **No runtime libraries** (Lean managed runtime) | Link line is freestanding C + small driver only; no `libleanshared` | Host Lake elaborate wall-clock |
| **Linear types help** | Workload uses linear mint/consume (exact-once, fail-closed double consume) and compose host_compose mint/consume; freestanding path is feasible without GC because ownership is exact-once | Counterfactual "same compiler with linear off"; vague compile-path slogan |
| **Fastest C** | Runtime ns/op of same logical work on freestanding vs named baselines, **per job class** | Compile seconds; merging mint ns/op with compose ns/op |
| **Provably** | Split: speed is empirical; **PROVABLY** in this repo is CompCert wire seal (correctness), not speed | Mash CompCert matrix into a speed proof |

---

## Methods

### Job classes (never merge ns/op across classes without labels)

| Job class | Logical work | N default env |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|
| **mint_consume** | Acquire resource once -> use -> release exactly once | `BENCH_RUNTIME_N` (default 200000000) |
| **compose** | Build small host-compose / node graph each op (push, edges, mint, mark, check, extract, consume) | `BENCH_RUNTIME_COMPOSE_N` (default 10000000) |
| **mint_consume (Lean)** | Same **logical** class under Lean managed runtime; **different** N | `BENCH_RUNTIME_LEAN_N` (default 50000000) |

Outer recipe: 1 discard process + `BENCH_RUNTIME_RUNS` (default 3) measured
processes; each process also warms once inside the driver. Report median ns/op
and mean ns/op from measured processes, plus **min / max / sample stdev** of
ns/op across measured runs after dropping the first sample when multi-run
(T2 spread; default RUNS=3 still works; raise RUNS for tighter stdev).
**Never merge ns/op across different N without labels.**

**Compose stage timers (T1, 2026-08-12):** freestanding compose smoke only
(`slake_runtime_bench_freestanding_compose.c`). After the primary whole-op timed
loop, a separate stage-attribution pass prints `stage_ns_per_op_*` for
init / push_nodes / edges / mint / mark / well_typed / check_fail_closed /
extract / consume / post_check, plus group rollups (setup, mint_mark, check,
extract_consume). Default ON; `BENCH_RUNTIME_STAGE_TIMERS=0` disables;
`BENCH_RUNTIME_STAGE_N` caps stage pass N (default min(compose N, 200000)).
Product wire under emit/out has **no** always-on timers. Living report section
**Compose stage timers**; stage ns includes `clock_gettime` overhead (relative
attribution, not absolute product claim).

**Machine-readable metrics (T4, 2026-08-12):** each full `just bench-runtime`
also writes `doc/BENCH-RUNTIME-metrics.tsv` (tab-separated; one row per arm;
columns stamp/arm/exit/job_class/N/ns_median/mean/min/max/stdev/wall/ops/outer_real).
Soft-skip arms appear as exit status. Human `doc/BENCH-RUNTIME-latest.md` remains
primary.

**Flag matrix (T3, 2026-08-12):** timing-link CFLAGS only via
`BENCH_RUNTIME_CFLAGS` (default `-O2`). Structural freestanding-first `-c` stays
fixed (`-O2 -ffreestanding -nostdlib`). Recipe `just bench-runtime-flag-matrix`
runs R-free mint under `-O2`, `-O3`, and optional `-O3 -flto` (LTO soft-skips on
link fail). Writes `doc/bench-history/flag-matrix-latest.tsv`. Default suite
remains `-O2` until E4. Research:
`doc/dev/research/runtime-flag-matrix-2026-08-12.md`.

**Baseline snapshot (T5, 2026-08-12):** living latest + metrics still overwrite.
`just bench-runtime-snapshot` copies metrics (and report) to
`doc/bench-history/<stamp>/` and tip `doc/BENCH-RUNTIME-baseline.tsv`. Map:
`doc/bench-history/README.md`.

**Structural no-GC gate polish (T8, 2026-08-12):** freestanding mint/compose print
`structural_gate=pass` or `fail_ldd` / `fail_nm` with matched lines; soft-skip
when ldd/nm missing; nm checks both `-D` and full symbol table. Not in default
`just check`.

### Arms

| Arm | Job class | Implementation | Link honesty |
|-----|-----------|----------------|--------------|
| **R-free** | mint_consume | `slake_consume_token_mint` then `slake_consume_token_consume` | emit + freestanding smoke only |
| **R-gc-shape** | mint_consume | `malloc` payload then `free` each op | driver only; baseline=**heap_churn** |
| **R-boehm** | mint_consume | `GC_INIT`; `GC_MALLOC` then `GC_FREE` | driver + `-lgc` / pkg-config bdw-gc; baseline=**boehm_gc**; soft-skip `skip_no_boehm` if no gc.h/libgc |
| **R-lean** (Arm C) | mint_consume (logical) | Lean `MintCell` ByteArray mint then discard (`runOpsIO`); `IO.monoNanosNow` | lake exe `slake-runtime-bench-lean`; baseline=**lean_managed_runtime**; soft-skip `skip_no_lake` / `skip_lean_build`; RT via libleanshared in ldd **or** embedded `lean_*` symbols/bytes (static layout) |
| **R-free-compose** | compose | `slake_host_compose_*` init/push/edge/mint/mark/check/extract/consume | emit + freestanding compose smoke only |
| **R-gc-shape-compose** | compose | malloc node list + edges + token; free all at end of op | driver only; baseline=**heap_churn** |

### Arm C methods (Lean managed runtime)

- **Not freestanding C IR.** Answers cost of a similar mint/consume-class
  protocol under classic Lean managed runtime / GC path.
- **Timed step:** process **run** only after **untimed** warm
  `lake build slake-runtime-bench-lean` (not cold full-package elaborate;
  that is the compile-path secondary suite).
- **Workload:** loop N times allocating a small structure (`MintCell` with
  `ByteArray`) and discarding it so the managed runtime path is exercised.
- **Metrics:** same key=value lines as C drivers (`N=`, `wall_seconds=`,
  `ns_per_op=`, `ops_per_s=`, `status=ok`, `baseline=lean_managed_runtime`,
  `job_class=mint_consume`).
- **N:** default `BENCH_RUNTIME_LEAN_N=50000000` (document separately from
  freestanding 2e8; ratios labeled when N differs).
- **Soft-skip:** no `lake` on PATH -> `status=skip_no_lake` exit 0; build/binary
  fail -> `status=skip_lean_build` exit 0.

### Structural checks (every freestanding arm)

- Wire present under `emit/` and `out/freestanding-c/` (`just build` if missing).
- Freestanding-first `cc -c` of wire (`-ffreestanding -nostdlib` preferred).
- Exact link line logged.
- `ldd` / `nm` when tools exist: fail honesty if leanshared / libgc / Boehm appear on R-free.
- Boehm arm: **must** show libgc in ldd when the arm runs (contrast).
- Lean arm: show Lean RT when run (shared libleanshared **or** embedded `lean_*`).
- Binary size recorded.
- In-driver contracts: mint/consume fail-closed; compose mint/consume fail-closed.

### What this does not claim

- Not "fastest C on Earth" or all of C.
- Not full elaborator parity.
- Not PROVABLY-as-speed.
- Does not flip free / complete / FullHost / full parity.
- heap_churn is **not** Boehm; boehm_gc is **not** Lean managed runtime.
- Lean managed runtime is **not** freestanding C IR (labeled contrast only).

---

## Causal line (honest)

Linear / affine discipline on the product path makes exact-once resources
expressible without a garbage collector. The freestanding wire exposes that as
`slake_consume_token_*` / `slake_host_compose_*`. The bench measures those paths
against named baselines:

1. **heap_churn** (libc malloc/free every op) -- optimized allocator path, not a GC.
2. **boehm_gc** (real Boehm) -- real GC library on the link line.
3. **lean_managed_runtime** -- classic Lean managed RT process run (Arm C);
   similar logical mint/consume; not the same C IR as freestanding.

On a thin mint/consume microbench, freestanding can lose to heap_churn (allocator
noise vs stack protocol). Against Boehm on the same mint-class job, freestanding
is much faster on this machine (no GC library overhead). Against Lean managed
runtime (labeled N), freestanding mint is also faster on this machine while
carrying **no** Lean RT on the consumer link. Compose-class still pays
freestanding API work vs a thin malloc node list. Ratio is empirical per job
class, N, and machine.

## Sample living numbers (2026-08-09 host run; re-run for your machine)

From `doc/BENCH-RUNTIME-latest.md` generated 2026-08-09 17:47:34 UTC:

| Job | Freestanding median ns/op | Baseline | Baseline median ns/op | Ratio baseline/free | N note |
|-----|--------------------------:|----------|----------------------:|--------------------:|--------|
| mint_consume | 1.9240 | heap_churn | 0.6365 | 0.331 | same N 2e8 |
| mint_consume | 1.9240 | boehm_gc | 18.0051 | 9.358 | same N 2e8 |
| mint_consume (labeled) | 1.9240 | lean_managed_runtime | 6.4591 | 3.357 | free N=2e8; lean N=5e7 |
| compose | 41.6512 | heap_churn compose | 10.4988 | 0.252 | same N 1e7 |

Interpretation: **no GC / no Lean runtime** on freestanding link is structural
and green. **Speed** vs heap_churn favors the libc path on these micro jobs;
**speed** vs Boehm and vs Lean managed (labeled) favors freestanding on
mint_consume. PROVABLY remains correctness only.
